query: Bally's is committed to paying for traffic mitigation, new bus stops, Ferry Point Park improvements and a ferry shuttle.

facts.text: Bally's committed to pay for traffic mitigation for its Bronx project.
Bally's agreed to fund additional bus stops for the project.
Bally's promised improvements to Ferry Point Park.
Bally's committed to support a ferry shuttle for the project.
The environmental findings require a construction traffic plan at least nine months before construction.
The Board described at least one new bus stop in the park and two at the facility.
A $160 million Ferry Point Park redesign was presented for community review.
The Public Design Commission listed the park reconstruction for preliminary review.
Bally's ferry shuttle service existed before this casino commitment.
The land transaction included an approximately $4.6 million construction and infrastructure easement.

conditions.text: Bally's paid for the promised Bronx traffic mitigation.
Bally's funded the promised new bus stops.
Bally's funded the promised Ferry Point Park improvements.
Bally's funded the promised ferry shuttle improvement beyond the existing service.

reference_verdict.reasoning: §5 decision order: (1) deliverables can be evidenced; (2) the passage states no due date, so 'not yet due' does not apply to the row as a whole; (3) no source contradicts a delivery claim (the MTA statement shows no plan, not a dispute); (4) independent sources (Gothamist, Time Out, Public Design Commission) confirm one part of the chain: the park improvements are in design and public review. They do not confirm Bally's paid for them or that any work began → partially corroborated. Other parts: traffic is defined and enforceable but tied to construction (not yet due); no evidence of new bus stops; the ferry shuttle predates the commitment and no expansion was found. Competing reading: not yet due (the current gold label), since the Board expects this work before opening (~2030). Recommend splitting into four records: park → partially corroborated; traffic → not yet due; bus stops → no public evidence located; shuttle → partially corroborated (existing service, expansion unconfirmed).

sources.title: GFLB selection document, Bally's Bronx: Board Evaluation
sources.specific_evidence: Source of the commitment (four deliverables, no amounts or dates).

sources.title: CEQR Statement of Findings, Bally's Bronx
sources.publisher: NYC Office of the Deputy Mayor for Housing, Economic Development and Workforce (Nov 17, 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Traffic measures defined: one-way Lafayette Ave overpass, signal changes, restriping, parking limits; Ring Road becomes a widened city street; Bally's duties go in the Contract of Sale with NYC Parks; construction traffic plan due to NYCDOT ≥9 months before construction. Bus stops and shuttle not addressed.
sources.notes: Traffic component: tied to construction, which has not started. Method D.

sources.title: GFLB final report and findings
sources.specific_evidence: Traffic improvements (Ring Road, sidewalks, overpass) expected before opening; at least 1 new bus stop in Ferry Point Park and 2 at the facility.
sources.notes: Gives the benchmark for bus stops. Method D.

sources.title: The Bronx is getting a new casino and a reimagined Ferry Point Park, too'
sources.specific_evidence: $160M park redesign (Hargreaves Jones) presented to CB10's parks committee; CB10 vote on a support letter set for Oct 15; also under Public Design Commission review; park construction not before 2028. Nearest bus stop ~30-min walk; MTA: 'premature to evaluate demand for transportation to a facility that has yet to be built.' Bally's has run a free ferry shuttle since 2023.
sources.notes: Independent source. Confirms park design progress; indicates no bus-stop work; shuttle predates the commitment. Method A snippet + Method B full text.

sources.title: This waterfront Bronx park could get a $160 million makeover'
Public Design Commission public agenda, Oct 20, 2026
sources.specific_evidence: Ferry Point Park reconstruction (western and northeastern portions) at preliminary review, sponsored by NYC Parks and DOT.
sources.notes: Independent. Bally's not named as funder, so the link to this commitment is inferred. Outcome not posted. Method D.

sources.title: Bally's land purchase coverage
sources.specific_evidence: Land deal included a ~$4.6M easement for construction access and infrastructure work; Bally's to make capital improvements to Ferry Point Park and Ring Road.
sources.notes: Easement is payment for access rights, not a park improvement.

sources.title: Bally's Bets on the Bronx' community benefits document
sources.specific_evidence: Lists a new Lafayette Ave overpass, rebuilt Ring Road, added MTA bus stops, expanded shuttle ($75M upfront).
sources.notes: Obligor's pledge, not a claim of delivery. No evidence the $75M was paid.

sources.title: NYC Parks capital project tracker #10479, Ferry Point Playground Reconstruction
sources.notes: Different funder; do not count toward Bally's commitment (failure code F11). The $160M redesign is not yet in the tracker.

sources.title: Bronx CB10 minutes (Apr 2026) and Oct 2026 calendar
sources.specific_evidence: Minutes posted only through Apr 2026; no Ferry Point/Bally's items. Outcome of the Oct 15, 2026 vote not yet posted.
sources.notes: The vote outcome is a known record that isn't public yet. Asked in the librarian request.
